title: Moby-Dick, Ch. 2 — The Carpet-Bag (Action Spine)
adaptation_principle: Prioritize Ishmael’s concrete travel, lodging hunt, and choices; fold rhetoric and digressions into captions without staging hypotheticals.

Ishmael.visual_description: Young adult seaman, lean and travel-worn; dark wool coat, rough scarf, simple trousers, scuffed patched boots; carries a small old brown carpet-bag under one arm; wind-reddened face.

Black Preacher.role: preacher at the church Ishmael enters by mistake
Black Preacher.visual_description: Middle-aged Black man in a plain dark coat at a simple wooden pulpit, one hand striking or holding a large dark book; stern, fervent posture.

Black Congregation.visual_description: Rows of Black men and women in plain winter clothing and caps, seated close together in a dim, smoky-lit meeting room, turning to look toward the doorway.

carpet_bag.visual_description: Small, old, brown fabric-and-leather carpet-bag with worn handles and scuffs.
carpet_bag.avoid_confusion: Do not depict as a hard suitcase or a seaman’s chest.

patched_boots.visual_description: Well-worn leather boots with visible sole wear and patches at the toes.
patched_boots.avoid_confusion: Do not render as new or fashionable boots.

inn_sign_spout.visual_description: Weathered wooden swinging sign with a painted white jet of spray; hangs by iron brackets and creaks in the wind.
inn_sign_spout.avoid_confusion: No readable text; do not replace the spray with a whale image.

ash_box.visual_description: Low wooden box half-full of grey ash in a dim porch; loose ash dust around it.
ash_box.avoid_confusion: Do not depict as a coal scuttle or metal trash can.

pulpit_and_book.visual_description: Plain wooden pulpit; large dark book with no readable text on the cover or pages.
pulpit_and_book.avoid_confusion: Do not adorn with ornate church symbols or readable scripture.

action_oriented_synopsis: I pack my carpet-bag, leave Manhattan for New Bedford, and find the Nantucket packet has sailed so I must wait till Monday. I resolve to sail only in a Nantucket craft, not from New Bedford. With little money and no acquaintances, I decide to find cheap lodgings for the two nights and to ask the price without being too particular. I tramp the freezing streets, pass the bright, costly inns, and head waterward for the cheapest houses. I enter a low public building, stumble over an ash-box, discover a negro church in full sermon, and back out. I come upon the Spouter Inn’s creaking sign, judge it cheap despite the ominous name, and prepare to go in.

caption_spine: I stuffed a shirt or two into my old carpet-bag, quit old Manhatto, reached New Bedford on a Saturday night in December, and learned the Nantucket packet had sailed—no reaching there till Monday.
My mind was made up to sail in no other than a Nantucket craft, so I would not ship from New Bedford.
With only a few pieces of silver and knowing no one, I must eat and sleep somewhere; so I told myself—be sure to inquire the price, and don’t be too particular.
I paced the dreary, icy streets, passed the jolly, expensive inns, and by instinct followed the ways waterward for the cheapest lodgings.
Entering a low, smoky-lighted building, I stumbled over an ash-box, saw a hundred black faces and a black preacher beating a book, and I backed out of ‘The Trap.’
At last I saw the swinging sign of the Spouter Inn—Peter Coffin—ominous, yet the dim, dilapidated house promised cheap lodgings; I scraped the ice from my feet to go in and see.

visual_safety_notes: Do not render any readable text on signs, books, or labels.
Treat the church scene with respect: avoid caricature; portray the preacher and congregation plainly and realistically.
Do not literalize metaphors (Tophet, Angel of Doom, Gomorrah, Lazarus, Dives); keep all supernatural or allegorical elements out of the imagery.
Avoid inserting ships, whales, or Nantucket identifiers not physically present in the scene.
